key_insight: DiffSimuQ transforms a broad class of sample-returning analog quantum experiments into executable derivative experiments whose expected outcomes equal the desired gradients.
engineering_relevance: Source and derivative experiments share a compiler that produces neutral-atom controls and selects between two gradient strategies using estimated cost.
method: Compositionally transform experiment programs into derivative programs in the same language.
Use the Nyquist shift rule for general time-dependent evolution, exploiting band-limited responses even with non-commuting controls.
Use a parameter-shift rule for involutory generators, inserting a parameter-independent operation at a sampled time.
evidence_signal: Machine-level noisy emulation reports avoidance of the finite-difference error floor, improved closed-loop optimization, and at most 0.3% additional source compilation time per derivative branch at 1,000 qubits.
watch_item: Exactness concerns expected outcomes; finite-shot uncertainty and hardware realization errors remain practical concerns, and reported evaluation uses emulation rather than physical-device experiments.
paper_title: Analog Quantum Experiments Meet Automatic Differentiation - from Programs to Atoms
